title: Set out nap cots three feet apart, head to toe
instruction: Set the two blue cots on your left and the two yellow cots on your right out in a row on the green mat, long sides pointing away from you and at least 9.2 cm apart, then put one pink pillow on an end of each cot, alternating ends from cot to cot so neighbours lie head to toe.
context: Childcare licensing rules require nap cots at least 3 ft from each other on every side, so staff can reach every child and germs spread less, with neighbouring children placed head to toe; staff set the room out to that rule before every nap. Done by: childcare workers, preschool teachers.
setup: A 1:10 scale nap room. A green rubber mat (22 cm front to back, 64 cm side to side, 2 mm thick) is fixed to the table between the arms, its centre 28 cm in front of the arm bases, so it spans 17 to 39 cm in front of them and 32 cm to each side of the middle. Outside it on each side a dark grey plastic storage strip (29 cm front to back, 8 cm side to side, 2 mm thick) is fixed with its centre 42 cm out from the middle and 26 cm in front of the bases. Four cots, rigid plastic boxes 12 cm long, 5.5 cm wide and 3 cm tall, 100 g each, lie flat on the strips with their long sides pointing away from the arms: two blue ones on the left strip and two yellow ones on the right strip, centred on the strip, their centres 19 and 33 cm in front of the bases. Four pink foam pillows (30 mm long, 45 mm wide, 22 mm tall, 30 g each) lie flat on the table 14 cm in front of the bases, 45 mm side pointing left to right: two on the left, their centres 27 and 34 cm left of the middle, and two on the right, 27 and 34 cm right of the middle. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Tilt is the angle between a box's top or bottom face and level, so a cot or pillow upside down counts as flat (they are plain boxes). A cot is set out when it is tilted at most 10 degrees, its bottom within 3 mm of the mat's top, its whole outline inside the mat, and its long side within 20 degrees of front to back: 0.05 each. A cot's outline is its rectangle seen from above; a cot tilted more than 10 degrees counts as its world-aligned bounding box seen from above. A set-out cot whose closest gap to every other cot, outline edge to outline edge (a cot still in the gripper included), is at least 9.2 cm (3 ft at 1:10): 0.1 more each. A pillow is on a cot when its centre is inside the cot's outline, its bottom from 1 cm below to 3 mm above the cot's top and it is tilted at most 20 degrees; it is on an end when its centre is at least 3 cm from the cot's centre along the cot's length, the far end (away from the arms) or the near end. Taking the set-out cots left to right as a row, a set-out cot with exactly one pillow, on an end, whose neighbours in the row (at least one) each have exactly one pillow on the opposite end: 0.1 each. All of it, four cots set out, spaced and head to toe: 1.0. The score is 0 if any cot or pillow is off the table; any cot is tilted more than 45 degrees; any cot is stacked on another: their outlines overlapping seen from above, its bottom from 1 cm below to 5 cm above the other's top (on it, or on one or two pillows on it), even while held; any cot lies on a pillow: their outlines overlapping seen from above, the cot's bottom within 1 cm of the pillow's top, even while held; any two cots whose centres are over the mat and whose bottoms are less than 3 cm above the mat's top, even while held, are less than 3 cm (1 ft at 1:10) apart edge to edge; or two neighbouring cots each have one pillow on the same end, where for this rule neighbours are adjacent cots, left to right, among all cots whose centres are over the mat, set out or not. A cot carried more than 3 cm above the mat and more than 5 cm above any cot below it counts for neither the stacking nor the pushed-together rule.
reset_notes: Lay the cots back on their strips, long sides pointing away from the arms, blue on the left and yellow on the right, and the pillows back at their four marks in front of the arm bases; tape outlines on the table make this quick.
fidelity: Approximate: a 1:10 model. Cots are solid rigid boxes, taller for their size than real cots (30 cm at full scale) so the gripper can hold them; pillows are rigid blocks. The cots are symmetric, so a pillow marks the head end. No children or bedding are modelled. The mat and strips are fixed (tape them down for real trials). Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
